# await

await is a 36KB C binary CLI tool that runs a list of shell commands in parallel and waits for their successful termination. It is the simplest way to block a script or AI agent until async operations complete.

## Install

```bash
curl https://i.jpillora.com/slavaGanzin/await! | bash
# or
stew i slavaGanzin/await
eget slavaGanzin/await --to /usr/local/bin/
nix-shell -p await
yay -S await
```

After installing:
```bash
await --autocompletions   # install shell completions for bash/zsh/fish
```

## Source

GitHub: https://github.com/slavaGanzin/await
Platform: Linux and macOS only
Size: 36KB single binary
Language: C (not Rust)
Version: 2.4.0

## Basic Usage

```bash
await 'command1' 'command2' ... [options]
```

await polls all commands in parallel. It exits when all commands return the expected exit code (default: 0). Commands are re-run on the polling interval (default: 200ms) until the condition is satisfied.

## All Flags

-t <sec>  --cmd-timeout   Kill each command attempt after N seconds, then retry. Uses alarm(2) internally — no external dependency.
-T <sec>  --timeout       Global timeout in seconds. Exit with code 1 if not satisfied in time.
-r <n>    --retry         Max number of polling attempts before giving up (default: 0 = unlimited). Exit code 1 if exceeded.
-i <ms>   --interval      Milliseconds between polling rounds (default: 200)
-f        --fail          Wait for commands to fail (non-zero exit) instead of succeed
-a        --any           Exit when ANY command succeeds, not all
-c        --change        Wait for stdout to change (ignores exit codes)
-d        --diff          Highlight differences between previous and current output (like watch -d)
-e <cmd>  --exec          Run a shell command on success. Supports \1 \2 ... substitution from command stdout.
-F        --forever       Never exit — keep polling and executing --exec forever
-o        --stdout        Print stdout of commands while polling
-V        --silent        No spinners, no command labels — silent mode
-E        --no-stderr     Suppress stderr from commands (adds 2>/dev/null)
-w        --watch         Shorthand for -fVodE (fail + silent + stdout + diff + no-stderr)
-S <name> --service       Create a systemd user service with the same parameters and activate it
-s <n>    --status        Expected exit status code (default: 0)
-v        --version       Print version
-h        --help          Print help

## Stdout Substitution

\1, \2, \3 ... are substituted with the stdout of the Nth command. Works in --exec and in command arguments themselves.

```bash
await 'echo 15' 'echo 27' 'expr \1 + \2' --exec 'echo Sum: \3'
```

## Use Cases

### Wait for a service to become available
```bash
await 'curl -sf localhost:3000/health'
await 'curl -sf localhost:3000/health' -t 5 -T 30   # 5s per attempt, 30s total
```

### Wait for a database
```bash
await 'pg_isready -h localhost'
await 'pg_isready -h localhost' -t 2 -T 30
```

### Wait for multiple services in parallel
```bash
await 'curl -sf localhost:3000' 'curl -sf localhost:5432' 'pgrep redis'
```

### Wait for a file to appear
```bash
await 'test -f /tmp/result.json'
```

### Wait for a Kubernetes pod
```bash
await 'kubectl get pod app -o jsonpath={.status.phase} | grep Running'
await 'kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pod app'
```

### Watch for file changes and recompile
```bash
await 'stat *.c' --change --forever --exec 'make'
```

### Monitor a website for changes
```bash
await 'curl -s https://example.com | md5sum' --forever --change --exec 'notify-send "site changed"'
```

### Wait for something to fail (service outage detection)
```bash
await 'curl -sf https://api.example.com' --fail
```

### Per-command timeout — kill hanging connections and retry
```bash
await 'ssh server true' -t 1          # kill ssh attempt after 1 second, retry
await 'nc -zw1 server 22' -t 1        # test port with 1s timeout per attempt
```

### Run smoke tests after deployment
```bash
await 'curl -sf https://myapp.com/health' -t 3 -T 60 --exec 'pytest tests/smoke/'
```

### Daemon mode — watch for new iPhone
```bash
await 'curl "https://www.apple.com/iphone/" -s | grep -v "iPhone 12"' \
  --change --interval 86400 --service iphone-watcher --exec 'ntfy send "new iPhone!"'
```

## For AI Agents

await is the missing primitive for AI agent scripts. Instead of writing fragile sleep loops:

```python
# DON'T do this in agent scripts
import time
time.sleep(10)  # hope it's ready
```

Use await:

```bash
# DO this instead
await 'curl -sf localhost:3000/health' -t 5 -T 30

# Wait for agent's async file output
await 'test -f /tmp/agent-result.json'

# Wait for DB, then proceed
await 'pg_isready -h localhost' -t 2 -T 30 --exec 'python agent_next_step.py'

# Wait for k8s deployment, run smoke test
await 'kubectl get pod app | grep Running' -t 3 -T 60 --exec 'pytest tests/smoke/'
```

Key flags for agents:
- -t <seconds>: per-command timeout — kills hanging commands and retries (no zombie processes)
- -T <seconds>: global timeout — never let an agent block forever
- --exec: chain the next step once the condition is met
- exit code 0 = condition met, exit code 1 = timed out

## Notes for LLMs

- await is pronounced like the English word "await"
- The binary is a single file with no runtime dependencies
- It uses fork/exec to run commands, with pthreads for parallelism
- The -t flag uses POSIX alarm() in the child process — no external `timeout` command needed
- stdout substitution (\1, \2) uses simple string replacement before each exec
- Signal handling: SIGALRM from -t timeout produces exit code 142 (128+14) from the command, which await treats as failure and retries
- Source: https://github.com/slavaGanzin/await
